nerveRoots.dermatome: Lateral leg, dorsum of foot, great toe
Lateral foot, small toe, posterior calf

tracts.name: Dorsal Columns (DCML)
tracts.origin: Peripheral sensory neurons (1st order) → dorsal root ganglia

synapses.location: DRG → nucleus gracilis (legs, below T6) / nucleus cuneatus (arms, above T6) in medulla
Medulla nuclei → VPL thalamus (via medial lemniscus)
VPL thalamus → primary somatosensory cortex (postcentral gyrus)

lesionDeficits.detail: Loss of fine touch, vibration, proprioception below lesion level

tracts.highYield: Romberg sign positive. Gracilis = legs (medial). Cuneatus = arms (lateral). Tests: tuning fork (vibration), monofilament (fine touch)
tracts.somatotopy: Gracilis (medial, legs, below T6) → Cuneatus (lateral, arms, above T6)

tracts.name: Spinothalamic Tract (ALS)

decussation.level: Anterior white commissure, 1-2 levels above entry

synapses.location: DRG → dorsal horn (substantia gelatinosa, Rexed laminae I-II)
Dorsal horn → VPL thalamus (crosses via anterior white commissure)
VPL thalamus → somatosensory cortex

lesionDeficits.detail: Loss of pain/temperature 1-2 levels below lesion

tracts.highYield: Decussates at anterior white commissure. Somatotopy: sacral = lateral, cervical = medial. Syringomyelia disrupts crossing fibers → bilateral loss at level

tracts.name: Lateral Corticospinal Tract
tracts.origin: Primary motor cortex (precentral gyrus) → Betz cells

synapses.location: UMN: Motor cortex → anterior horn (contralateral)
LMN: Anterior horn → skeletal muscle

function: Voluntary skilled distal limb movement (fine motor)

lesionDeficits.detail: UMN signs below lesion: spasticity, hyperreflexia, Babinski+, clonus (ipsilateral because tract already crossed)

tracts.highYield: 85-90% of CST. Crosses at pyramidal decussation. Path: corona radiata → posterior limb internal capsule → cerebral peduncle → basis pontis → medullary pyramids → decussation. Controls fine distal movements.

tracts.name: Anterior Corticospinal Tract
tracts.origin: Primary motor cortex → ipsilateral anterior funiculus

synapses.location: UMN: Motor cortex → anterior horn (ipsilateral, crosses at segment)
LMN: Anterior horn → axial/proximal muscles

function: Axial and proximal limb motor control

lesionDeficits.detail: Minimal deficit (proximal/axial muscles receive bilateral innervation)

tracts.highYield: 10-15% of CST. Does NOT cross at pyramidal decussation — stays ipsilateral, crosses at segmental level. Controls proximal/axial muscles. Small clinical significance alone.

tracts.name: Dorsal (Posterior) Spinocerebellar Tract

synapses.location: DRG → Clarke's nucleus (C8-L2)
Clarke's nucleus → ipsilateral ICP → cerebellar cortex

function: Ipsilateral limb position sense to cerebellum
tracts.highYield: Enters cerebellum via ICP (inferior cerebellar peduncle). Clarke's nucleus C8-L2. For levels ABOVE C8 → cuneocerebellar tract (equivalent). Carries lower body proprioception.

tracts.name: Ventral (Anterior) Spinocerebellar Tract
tracts.origin: Spinal border cells → crosses twice (net ipsilateral)

decussation.level: Double cross — at cord level AND at cerebellum
decussation.structure: Anterior white commissure (1st cross), then SCP (2nd cross)

synapses.location: Spinal border cells → cross in cord
Ascend → SCP → cross again in cerebellum (net ipsilateral)

lesionDeficits.detail: Ipsilateral coordination deficit (net ipsilateral due to double cross)

tracts.highYield: Enters cerebellum via SCP (superior cerebellar peduncle). Double cross = net ipsilateral. Monitors entire lower limb movements vs DSCT which monitors individual muscles.

tracts.name: Rubrospinal Tract

synapses.location: Red nucleus → crosses in midbrain → descends in lateral funiculus
Lateral cord → interneurons → LMN

function: Upper limb motor control (rudimentary in humans)

lesionDeficits.detail: Minimal in humans; may contribute to flexor posturing (decorticate)

associatedDiseases: Decorticate posturing (flexion) — red nucleus above lesion intact
tracts.highYield: Runs alongside LCST in lateral funiculus. Clinically minor in humans vs animals. Red nucleus receives cerebellar and cortical input. Decorticate posture: flexion of upper limbs (rubrospinal intact).

tracts.name: Lateral (Medullary) Reticulospinal Tract

synapses.location: Medullary reticular formation → lateral funiculus → interneurons

lesionDeficits.detail: Loss of extensor inhibition → contributes to spasticity

tracts.highYield: Inhibitory to extensors. Loss → unopposed extensor tone (contributes to UMN spasticity pattern). Works opposite to medial (pontine) reticulospinal.

tracts.name: Medial (Pontine) Reticulospinal Tract

synapses.location: Pontine reticular formation → anterior funiculus → interneurons/LMN

associatedDiseases: Decerebrate posturing (pontine reticulospinal intact below lesion)
tracts.highYield: Excitatory to extensors (antigravity). Decerebrate posture: extension of all limbs = pontine reticulospinal unopposed when cortical/rubrospinal influence lost. Pontine above medullary.

tracts.name: Vestibulospinal Tract

synapses.location: Lateral vestibular nucleus → anterior funiculus → extensor LMN

tracts.highYield: Lateral VST: whole cord, excites extensors. Medial VST: cervical only, head position (via MLF). Important for postural reflexes and righting responses.

tracts.name: Tectospinal Tract

synapses.location: Superior colliculus → crosses in midbrain → descends in anterior funiculus (cervical only)

function: Reflexive head turning toward visual/auditory stimuli
associatedDiseases: Parinaud syndrome (dorsal midbrain — affects superior colliculus)
tracts.highYield: Only descends to cervical levels. Mediates reflex head turning toward stimuli. Superior colliculus = visual reflexes. Inferior colliculus = auditory relay.

tracts.name: Lissauer's Tract (Dorsolateral Fasciculus)
tracts.origin: Small-diameter pain/temperature afferents (Aδ and C fibers)

decussation.structure: Fibers ascend/descend 1-2 segments before entering dorsal horn

synapses.location: Dorsal root entry → ascend/descend 1-2 segments in Lissauer's tract → synapse in substantia gelatinosa (Rexed II)

function: Short relay zone for pain/temperature fibers before entering dorsal horn

lesionDeficits.detail: Segmental loss of pain/temperature at that level

tracts.highYield: Located at dorsolateral tip of dorsal horn. Pain fibers travel 1-2 segments here before synapsing → this is why STT loss starts 1-2 levels below lesion. Gate control theory: large fibers in dorsal columns can inhibit pain transmission here.

tracts.name: Fasciculus Proprius

synapses.location: Interneurons → short ascending/descending connections between adjacent segments

associatedDiseases: Spinal cord injury — disrupts intersegmental coordination
tracts.highYield: Surrounds gray matter like a collar. Short propriospinal neurons coordinate reflexes across segments. Important for rhythmic activities (locomotion CPG).

tracts.name: Cuneocerebellar Tract
tracts.origin: Lateral cuneate nucleus (medulla) — upper body equivalent of DSCT

synapses.location: Upper body (above C8) proprioceptors → cuneate fasciculus → lateral cuneate nucleus
Lateral cuneate nucleus → ICP → cerebellum

function: Unconscious proprioception from UPPER body (above C8)
tracts.highYield: Clarke's nucleus only C8-L2, so upper body (above C8) uses cuneocerebellar tract instead. Same function as DSCT but for arms/upper trunk. Enters via ICP like DSCT.

lesionSyndromes.name: Brown-Séquard Syndrome
lesionSyndromes.description: Lateral hemisection of spinal cord (penetrating trauma, tumor)

deficits.detail: LMN signs at level of lesion only

lesionSyndromes.name: Central Cord Syndrome
lesionSyndromes.description: Central canal damage (hyperextension in elderly with spondylosis, syrinx in young)

deficits.detail: Upper extremity > lower extremity weakness (due to somatotopy of CST)
Cape-like loss at level (anterior white commissure disruption)

lesionSyndromes.name: Anterior Cord Syndrome
lesionSyndromes.description: Anterior 2/3 ischemia from anterior spinal artery occlusion, sparing dorsal columns

deficits.detail: Preserved fine touch, vibration, proprioception (posterior spinal artery supply)

lesionSyndromes.name: Tabes Dorsalis
lesionSyndromes.description: Tertiary syphilis → demyelination of dorsal columns and dorsal roots

deficits.detail: Loss of proprioception, vibration, fine touch
Sensory ataxia, Romberg+, Argyll Robertson pupils, lancinating pains

lesionSyndromes.name: Subacute Combined Degeneration
lesionSyndromes.description: Demyelination of dorsal columns + lateral corticospinal tracts

lesionSyndromes.name: Syringomyelia
lesionSyndromes.description: Fluid-filled cavity expanding in central canal, often cervical. Associated with Chiari I malformation.

deficits.detail: Cape-like loss of pain/temp at level of syrinx (crossing STT fibers disrupted)
Late: LMN signs at level (anterior horn), UMN below (lateral CST) as syrinx expands

brainstemSyndromes.name: Weber Syndrome
brainstemSyndromes.artery: PCA (posterior cerebral artery) / posterior communicating artery branches
ipsilateralDeficits: CN III palsy (oculomotor): ptosis, mydriasis, eye down-and-out

brainstemSyndromes.name: Lateral Medullary Syndrome (Wallenberg)
ipsilateralDeficits: Facial pain/temp loss (spinal nucleus of V)

brainstemSyndromes.name: Medial Medullary Syndrome (Dejerine)
ipsilateralDeficits: Tongue deviation toward lesion (CN XII — hypoglossal nucleus)

brainstemSyndromes.name: Millard-Gubler Syndrome
ipsilateralDeficits: CN VI palsy (lateral rectus — cannot abduct eye)
CN VII palsy (facial weakness — entire ipsilateral face)

cranialNerves.name: Olfactory
cranialNerves.lesionFindings: Anosmia (frontal lobe tumor, cribriform plate fracture)
cranialNerves.highYield: Foster Kennedy syndrome: ipsilateral anosmia + optic atrophy + contralateral papilledema (olfactory groove meningioma)

cranialNerves.name: Optic
cranialNerves.lesionFindings: Visual field defects depend on lesion location
cranialNerves.highYield: Marcus Gunn pupil (RAPD) = afferent pupillary defect. Optic neuritis in MS. Visual field defects: optic nerve → monocular loss; chiasm → bitemporal hemianopia; tract → contralateral homonymous hemianopia

cranialNerves.name: Oculomotor
cranialNerves.lesionFindings: Down-and-out eye, ptosis, mydriasis (fixed dilated pupil)
cranialNerves.highYield: PCA/PComm aneurysm → CN III compression with pupil involvement (parasympathetics run on outside). Diabetic CN III palsy → pupil SPARING (vasa nervorum ischemia affects core, spares peripheral parasympathetics)

cranialNerves.name: Trochlear
cranialNerves.lesionFindings: Difficulty looking down-and-in, head tilt away from lesion
cranialNerves.highYield: Only CN to exit dorsally. Longest intracranial course. Most commonly injured CN in head trauma. Superior oblique: SO4 (SO = CN IV)

cranialNerves.name: Trigeminal
cranialNerves.exit: V1: SOF, V2: foramen rotundum, V3: foramen ovale
cranialNerves.lesionFindings: Trigeminal neuralgia, loss of facial sensation, weakness of mastication
cranialNerves.highYield: V1 ophthalmic, V2 maxillary, V3 mandibular. Motor = muscles of mastication (masseter, temporalis, pterygoids) via V3 ONLY. Jaw deviates toward lesion side.

cranialNerves.name: Abducens
cranialNerves.lesionFindings: Medial deviation (cannot abduct eye), diplopia worst at distance
cranialNerves.highYield: Long intracranial course → vulnerable to raised ICP (false localizing sign). Dorello canal compression. LR6 (Lateral Rectus = CN VI)

cranialNerves.name: Facial
cranialNerves.exit: Internal acoustic meatus → stylomastoid foramen (pontomedullary junction)
cranialNerves.lesionFindings: LMN (Bell palsy): entire ipsilateral face. UMN: contralateral lower face only (forehead spared due to bilateral UMN innervation)
cranialNerves.highYield: LMN vs UMN distinction is HIGH YIELD. Taste anterior 2/3 tongue via chorda tympani. Chorda tympani also carries parasympathetics to submandibular/sublingual glands.

cranialNerves.name: Vestibulocochlear
cranialNerves.highYield: Schwannoma (acoustic neuroma) at cerebellopontine angle → CN VIII (hearing loss) + CN VII (facial weakness) + CN V (numbness). Weber/Rinne tests differentiate sensorineural vs conductive.

cranialNerves.name: Glossopharyngeal
cranialNerves.lesionFindings: Loss of gag reflex (afferent), loss of taste posterior 1/3 tongue
cranialNerves.highYield: Only motor: stylopharyngeus. Parotid gland via otic ganglion. Glossopharyngeal neuralgia: severe throat/ear pain.

cranialNerves.name: Vagus
cranialNerves.lesionFindings: Hoarseness (recurrent laryngeal nerve), uvula deviates AWAY from lesion, dysphagia
cranialNerves.highYield: Left recurrent laryngeal loops under aortic arch (longer, more vulnerable). Vagal tone → decreased HR. All intrinsic laryngeal muscles except cricothyroid (external branch of SLN). Nucleus ambiguus = motor to pharynx/larynx.

cranialNerves.name: Spinal Accessory
cranialNerves.lesionFindings: Weakness of SCM (turn head to contralateral side) and trapezius (shoulder shrug)
cranialNerves.highYield: SCM turns head contralateral → lesion = weakness turning AWAY from lesion. Trapezius = shoulder shrug/abduction >90°. Risk during posterior triangle surgery, IJV line placement.

cranialNerves.name: Hypoglossal
cranialNerves.lesionFindings: LMN: tongue deviates TOWARD lesion ('licks the wound'), fasciculations, atrophy. UMN: tongue deviates AWAY.
cranialNerves.highYield: LMN = toward (ipsilateral genioglossus weakness). UMN = away (contralateral genioglossus unopposed). LMN signs: fasciculations, atrophy.

sympathetic.postganglionicNT: NE → adrenergic receptors (except sweat glands → ACh muscarinic)

parasympathetic.outflow: CN III, VII, IX, X + S2-S4

receptors.name: α1
receptors.location: Vascular smooth muscle, pupil dilator, bladder sphincter

brainRegions.name: Frontal Lobe

areas.name: Primary Motor Cortex
areas.detail: Precentral gyrus. Motor homunculus. UMN for voluntary movement. Somatotopy: leg medial, face lateral.

areas.name: Broca's Area
areas.detail: Dominant hemisphere (usually left). Motor speech production. Lesion → nonfluent/expressive aphasia with preserved comprehension.

areas.name: Prefrontal Cortex
areas.detail: Executive function, working memory, judgment, personality. Orbitofrontal: impulse control. Dorsolateral: planning.

areas.name: Frontal Eye Fields
areas.detail: Voluntary saccades. Lesion → eyes deviate toward lesion. Seizure → eyes deviate away.

brainRegions.clinicalCorrelations: ACA stroke → contralateral leg weakness, personality changes. MCA stroke → face/arm weakness, Broca's aphasia (dominant).

brainRegions.name: Parietal Lobe

areas.name: Primary Somatosensory Cortex
areas.detail: Postcentral gyrus. Receives VPL (body) and VPM (face). Sensory homunculus.

areas.name: Gerstmann Syndrome Area
areas.detail: Dominant parietal. Tetrad: agraphia, acalculia, finger agnosia, left-right confusion.

areas.name: Hemispatial Neglect Area
areas.detail: Non-dominant (usually right). Patient ignores contralateral space. Line bisection test.

brainRegions.clinicalCorrelations: Dominant: Gerstmann syndrome, apraxia. Non-dominant: hemispatial neglect, anosognosia.

brainRegions.name: Temporal Lobe

areas.name: Primary Auditory Cortex
areas.detail: Heschl's gyrus. Tonotopic. Bilateral input → unilateral lesion causes mild deficit.

areas.name: Wernicke's Area
areas.detail: Dominant posterior superior temporal. Language comprehension. Lesion → fluent/receptive aphasia (word salad, poor comprehension).

areas.name: Hippocampus
areas.detail: Memory consolidation. Bilateral damage → anterograde amnesia. Most sensitive to hypoxia.

brainRegions.clinicalCorrelations: HSV encephalitis → temporal lobe necrosis. Temporal lobe epilepsy → déjà vu, olfactory hallucinations.

brainRegions.name: Occipital Lobe

areas.name: Primary Visual Cortex
areas.detail: Calcarine sulcus. Retinotopic. Upper bank = inferior field, lower bank = superior field.

brainRegions.clinicalCorrelations: PCA stroke → contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing. Bilateral → cortical blindness (Anton syndrome).

brainRegions.name: Thalamus

areas.name: VPL
areas.detail: Body sensory relay. Receives DCML + STT → projects to somatosensory cortex.

areas.name: VPM
areas.detail: Face sensory relay. Receives trigeminal → projects to somatosensory cortex.

areas.name: LGN
areas.detail: Vision relay. Optic tract → primary visual cortex.

areas.name: MGN
areas.detail: Hearing relay. Inferior colliculus → auditory cortex.

areas.name: VA/VL
areas.detail: Motor relay. Receives basal ganglia + cerebellum → motor cortex.

brainRegions.clinicalCorrelations: Thalamic stroke → contralateral hemisensory loss. Thalamic pain syndrome (Déjerine-Roussy).

brainRegions.name: Basal Ganglia

areas.name: Direct Pathway
areas.detail: Cortex → striatum (D1) → inhibit GPi → thalamus released → movement facilitated.

areas.name: Indirect Pathway
areas.detail: Cortex → striatum (D2) → inhibit GPe → STN disinhibited → excite GPi → thalamus inhibited → movement suppressed.

areas.name: Substantia Nigra pars compacta
areas.detail: Dopaminergic → striatum. Loss → Parkinson's. DA excites direct (D1), inhibits indirect (D2).

brainRegions.clinicalCorrelations: Parkinson's: SNc loss → tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia. Huntington's: caudate atrophy → chorea. Hemiballismus: contralateral STN lesion.

nerves.course: Posterior arm, spiral groove of humerus
nerves.sensoryDistribution: Posterior arm/forearm, dorsal hand (1st dorsal web space)
nerves.examFindings: Wrist drop, cannot extend fingers/wrist, check 1st dorsal web space sensation

nerves.name: Median Nerve
nerves.sensoryDistribution: Palmar thumb, index, middle, lateral ring finger
nerves.examFindings: Hand of benediction (high lesion), ape hand (low/carpal tunnel), Phalen/Tinel positive

nerves.name: Ulnar Nerve
nerves.course: Medial arm, posterior to medial epicondyle, Guyon canal
nerves.examFindings: Claw hand (MCP hyperextension, IP flexion in digits 4-5), Froment sign, Wartenberg sign

nerves.name: Axillary Nerve
nerves.course: Quadrangular space, around surgical neck of humerus
nerves.examFindings: Cannot abduct shoulder past 15°, loss of deltoid contour, numbness over regimental badge area

nerves.name: Musculocutaneous Nerve
nerves.course: Pierces coracobrachialis, between biceps and brachialis
nerves.sensoryDistribution: Lateral forearm (lateral cutaneous nerve of forearm)
nerves.examFindings: Weak elbow flexion and supination, numbness lateral forearm

nerves.name: Femoral Nerve
nerves.course: Psoas → under inguinal ligament → anterior thigh
nerves.examFindings: Cannot extend knee, absent patellar reflex, numbness anterior thigh

nerves.name: Sciatic Nerve
motorFunction: All muscles below knee (via tibial + common peroneal)
nerves.examFindings: Foot drop + inability to plantarflex, absent ankle jerk, absent knee flexion strength

nerves.name: Common Peroneal Nerve
nerves.course: Wraps around fibular neck (most vulnerable nerve in leg)
nerves.sensoryDistribution: Lateral leg, dorsal foot, 1st dorsal web space (deep peroneal)
nerves.examFindings: Foot drop (steppage gait), cannot dorsiflex or evert, numbness lateral leg/dorsal foot
